newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.S. politicians to suggest more aid for Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. politicians to suggest more aid for Cambodia.

text.p: A U.S. Congress delegation will recommend an increase in aid to Cambodia, saying their fears about human rights and environmental abuses had been allayed during a fact-finding mission to the developing nation.

"Obviously, we have ongoing concerns about human rights, press freedom, the environment, including logging and the like. I think they have been allayed fairly well by the discussions we have had," House of Representatives delegation head John Porter told reporters late on Wednesday at the end of a three-day visit.

"Our impression is that the intentions are there to address those issues forcefully," the Illinois Republican said of meetings with co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, adding: "The question...is whether you can carry out those intentions."

"We feel that there's a sensitivity...on the human rights issue, press freedom, logging and environmental issues," said Porter, who had expressed concerns about these issues on arriving in the Cambodian capital on Monday.

Porter said the delegation, which will report back to Congress on their findings, would like to increase U.S. aid to Cambodia "substantially". Washington currently grants Cambodia annual aid of about $40 million.

"We would like to get the numbers up. We feel that the United States ought to continue the human rights funding that we have, the democracy funding that we have...we'd like to see more funding to build some infrastructure like highways and we'd like to do better if we can on the mine-clearing."
Their input could affect decisions on U.S. aid and the granting of Generalised System of Preferences trade status, which lowers or eliminates trade tariffs.
Porter said delegates had met local human rights groups and felt there had been significant progress in this area, and that events were moving in the right direction.
But he added that the United States must continue to monitor progress in democracy and human rights in Cambodia.
